record.context_brief: How many triangles must concentrate on one edge in a dense graph?
record.original_question: Fix a constant c > 0. For a graph on n vertices with cn^2 edges, assume every edge belongs to at least one triangle. Let f(n; c) be the largest integer such that some edge of the graph is contained in at least f(n; c) triangles. Determine f(n; c) as sharply as possible, from above and below, as a function of n and c.

evidence.quote: Estimate f(n ; c) as well as possible both from above and below.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a constant $c>0$. For each integer $n\ge 1$, consider all simple graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices with at least $cn^2$ edges such that every edge of $G$ belongs to at least one triangle (a triangle being a set of three pairwise adjacent vertices). Define
\[
 f(n;c) \;=\; \min_{G}\;\max_{e\in E(G)} \, t_G(e),
\]
where $t_G(e)$ denotes the number of triangles in $G$ containing the edge $e$, the minimum is taken over all such graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices, and the maximum is taken over all edges $e$ of $G$. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $f(n;c)$ as $n\to\infty$ as sharply as possible, providing matching upper and lower bounds as functions of $n$ and $c$.
artifact.category_tag: extremal graph theory: triangles per edge
artifact.status_search_result: For c < 1/4, Fox and Loh (2012) showed that f(n;c) = n^{O(1/log log n)}, refuting the conjecture that f(n;c) > n^ε for some ε>0. For c > 1/4, a classical result guarantees an edge in at least n/6 triangles. So qualitatively the question is largely resolved (the polynomial growth conjecture is disproved and matching super-polylogarithmic lower bounds are known), but the precise asymptotic behavior of f(n;c) is not fully pinned down, so the sharp form remains open.

status_evidence.title: On a problem of Erdős and Rothschild on edges in triangles
status_evidence.snippet: Fox and Loh prove h(n,c) = n^{O(1/log log n)} for every fixed c < 1/4, disproving Erdős's conjecture that h(n,c) > n^ε.
status_evidence.claim: The polynomial-growth conjecture is disproved; sharp super-polylogarithmic upper bound established.

status_evidence.title: On a problem of Erdős and Rothschild on edges in triangles | Combinatorica
status_evidence.snippet: Erdös asked whether for every c>0 there is ε>0 such that h(n,c)>n^ε; the answer is negative.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the qualitative form of the question but matching bounds are not tight.
